shift_rule.core: competency is core if base >= 3 or id in leadership_class
shift_rule.up: core: +0.5 per level above anchor; support: 0
shift_rule.down: core: -1.0 per level below anchor; support: -0.5; floor 0, cap 4, round to 0.5
shift_rule.zero: base 0 stays 0 at every level (not required)

transfer.pair_key: FROMFAMILY>TOFAMILY, with FROMFAMILY>* as a wildcard
transfer.label: model; the four lead anchors (writing D<->P 0.8, research D<->M 0.7, brand strategy 0.6, analytics M->D 0.4) are the author's brief, not research; the 12 HR and OD rows (H is HR practice, O is HR consulting, transformation and OD) are my estimates from the 2026-10-21 research notes (handoff-docs/specs/hr-od-domain-research.md), not published weights. Same family counts 0.9 for every competency, so the differences between a generalist, an HR business partner, a recruiter and an L&D specialist enter through their vectors and their evidenced levels, not through the matrix

self_cap.level: min(level, max(0, target - 1)) until an artifact or test exists
self_cap.reading: The author to confirm (spec section 8, item 5)

waypoints.threshold_label: model: any value between 26.4 (brand designer M to creative director L, no waypoint in the spec) and 37.3 (PR associate to head of comms, waypoint in the spec) fits the worked examples
waypoints.rule: first candidate with a computable vector, a lower level than the target (same role) or a different role, and a distance below both the threshold and the target distance
